call_goal: Review the proposal with Granite Peak Credit Union after a successful pilot and agree a path to purchase
desired_outcomes: Understand the real budget constraint and timing
Agree what happens between now and the new fiscal year
Keep the deal alive without non-standard concessions

transcript.text: So that's the proposal. It's scoped to the member-support assistant like we discussed, and the two other teams would come on later if it makes sense. How's that landing?
Yeah. Um. So, okay. Let me just be straight with you.

The pilot was good. The team liked it, Ana's team especially, I'm not going to pretend otherwise. But I went to finance last week and there's, there's just nothing for this until next fiscal. Our year starts February first. It's, uh, it's not a no. It's a not now.
And I know you've probably got a quarter to close, so, sorry about that. I wanted to tell you before you, you know, built a forecast around it.
No, I really appreciate you telling me.

knowledge.title: Objection handling: budget timing
knowledge.text: When a buyer says there is no budget until a later period: acknowledge it, separate timing from priority, learn what their budget process requires (business case, approvers, dates), and agree what happens between now and then. Do not offer discounts or non-standard terms without deal-desk approval.

unacceptable_behaviors: Offers a discount, free extension, deferred billing or other special terms to pull the deal into this quarter
Quotes a price or contract terms
Mentions Keith's quarter, quota or forecast as a reason for the buyer to act
Treats 'not now' as a lost deal or as a 'no'
Asserts pain the pilot didn't establish (the buyer said only that the team liked it)
acceptable_questions: Appreciate that. What does getting this into the February budget actually involve on your side, and is there anything I can put together to help?
When you say not now, is it purely timing, or is there something that would need to change for it to make the February plan?
